353638.title: L1 convergence for greedy lattice paths
353638.literal_statement:
Let $\{X_{v}:v\in\mathbb{Z}^d\}$ be i.i.d. random variables, and let $M_n$ denote the maximum weight of a lattice path of length $n$ from the origin. Assume that there exists $\alpha>0$ such that

$$
E(X_0^{+})^d(\log^{+}X_0^{+})^{d+\alpha})<+\infty
$$

and that

$$
\int_{0}^{+\infty}P(X_0< -t)^{2d}\,\mathrm{d}t<+\infty.
$$

**$L^1$ convergence conjecture.** There exists a constant $M\in(-\infty,+\infty)$ such that

$$
E|M_n/n-M|\overset{n\to\infty}{\to}0.
$$

The stated negative-tail integrability condition ensures that $EM_n>-infty$; the conjectured $L^1$ convergence for greedy lattice paths is presented as an open problem requiring new ideas beyond the lattice-animal argument.
353638.source_name: Yinshan Chang and Anqi Zheng, “Greedy lattice paths with general weights”, arXiv:2202.07558 (2024).

353706.title: Cranston's maximum-average-degree conjecture for odd colorings
353706.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $\operatorname{mad}(G)$ be the maximum of $\frac{2|E(H)|}{|V(H)|}$ over all non-empty subgraphs $H$ of $G$, and let $\chi_o(G)$ be the least positive integer $c$ for which $G$ has a proper $c$-coloring in which every vertex of positive degree has some color appearing an odd number of times among its neighbors. **Cranston's conjecture.** For $c\geq 4$, if

$$
\operatorname{mad}(G)\leq\frac{4c-4}{c+1},
$$

then $\chi_o(G)\leq c$. Cranston proved this conjecture for $c\in\{5,6\}$, while the cases $c\geq 4$ in general remain open. It gives a sharp-looking sparsity threshold guaranteeing an odd coloring.
353706.source_name: Eun-Kyung Cho, Ilkyoo Choi, Hyemin Kwon and Boram Park, “Odd coloring of sparse graphs and planar graphs”, arXiv:2202.11267 (2022).

353711.title: The extremal sparsity conjecture for minimally globally rigid graphs
353711.literal_statement:
Let $d$ be a positive integer and let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph on at least $d+2$ vertices that is minimally globally rigid in $\mathbb{R}^d$. **The extremal sparsity conjecture.**

$$
|E|\leq (d+1)|V|-\binom{d+2}{2}
$$

and the minimum degree of $G$ is at most $2d+1$. This conjecture concerns sharp sparsity bounds for minimally globally rigid graphs; the paper's abstract and introduction state that it is answered affirmatively, so its database status is solved.
353711.source_name: Dániel Garamvölgyi and Tibor Jordán, “Minimally globally rigid graphs”, arXiv:2202.11617 (2022).

353749.title: Tensor-product Fourier dual-certificate conjecture for Hadamard matrices
353749.literal_statement:
Let $U(d)$ be the unitary group, let $\nu$ be normalized Haar measure on $U(d)$, let $e$ be its identity, and let $\mu_{[\bm H]}$ be the smoothed measure associated with the equivalence class of a Hadamard matrix $\bm H\in U(d)$. **Dual-certificate conjecture.** For every $d$, there exists a Hadamard matrix $\bm H\in U(d)$ such that

$$
\delta_e+d\mu_{[\bm H]}\succeq(d+1)\nu,
$$

or equivalently, $\widehat{\mu_{[\bm H]}}(\pi)\succeq-\frac1d\bm I$ for every irreducible representation $\pi$ of $U(d)$. If $d=p_1^{k_1}\cdots p_m^{k_m}$ is the prime factorization of $d$, one can take

$$
\bm H=\bigotimes_{k=1}^m\bm F_{p_k}^{\otimes k_k}.
$$

Such a certificate would imply the conjectured dimension-independent lower bound $B(d)=d+1$. The construction is motivated by observed tensor-product patterns in known mutually unbiased bases, but its validity remains to be verified.
353749.source_name: Afonso S. Bandeira, Nikolaus Doppelbauer and Dmitriy Kunisky, “Dual bounds for the positive definite functions approach to mutually unbiased bases”, arXiv:2202.13259 (2022).

353765.title: Second-order ground-state energy conjecture for the Gross–Pitaevskii three-body Bose gas
353765.literal_statement:
Let $H_N^{\rm GP}$ be the Gross–Pitaevskii Hamiltonian, let $E_{\rm GP}(N)$ denote its ground-state energy, and let $e_{\rm GP}$ be the minimum of the corresponding Gross–Pitaevskii energy functional. Then **Ground-state energy conjecture.**

$$
E_{\rm GP}(N)=Ne_{\rm GP}+N^{1/2}C^{(2)}_{\rm GP}+\mathcal O(1),
$$

for some constant $C^{(2)}_{\rm GP}$ independent of $N$. The authors explain that an upper bound of the expected order appears accessible, but obtaining the matching lower bound and identifying the constant remain open.
353765.source_name: Phan Thành Nam, Julien Ricaud and Arnaud Triay, “Dilute Bose gas with three-body interaction: recent results and open questions”, arXiv:2202.13967 (2022).

353767.title: Gross–Pitaevskii limit conjecture for combined two- and three-body interactions
353767.literal_statement:
Let $H_N^{\rm Comb}$ be the Hamiltonian with two-body potential $W$ at scaling parameter $\beta=1$ and three-body potential $V$. Let $e^{\rm Comb}_{\rm GP}(b_1,b_2)$ be the minimum of the combined Gross–Pitaevskii functional, let $b(W)$ be the scattering energy of $W$, and let $b_{\mathcal M}(V)$ be the three-body scattering parameter. Then **Combined-interaction Gross–Pitaevskii conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\inf\sigma(H_N^{\rm Comb})}{N}=e^{\rm Comb}_{\rm GP}\left(b(W),b_{\mathcal M}(V)\right).
$$

The case $\beta=1$ is challenging because both interactions are critically scaled, so correlations at both the two- and three-body levels contribute to the leading order. The limit remains open.
353767.source_name: Phan Thành Nam, Julien Ricaud and Arnaud Triay, “Dilute Bose gas with three-body interaction: recent results and open questions”, arXiv:2202.13967 (2022).

353808.title: Thomas-Yau's minimizer-to-special-Lagrangian conjecture
353808.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the admissible class of Lagrangian currents and let $\mathcal{S}$ be the Solomon functional. 353823.title: Partial arithmetic-periodicity conjecture for Family B cut games
353823.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a non-empty set of even numbers, each at least $4$, and let $Y$ be a non-empty set of odd numbers, each at least $5$. Let $x$ and $y$ be the smallest elements of $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Family B consists of cut sets

$$
\mathcal{C}=\{1\}\cup X\cup Y.
$$

**Family B partial conjecture.** If $3x<y$, then

$$
\mathcal{G}_{\mathcal{C}}(n)=\mathcal{G}_{\{1,x\}}(n)
$$

for $n\geq 1$. The paper presents this as a partial extension of the known result for two-element cut sets and notes that no full conjecture is available for Family B; proving arithmetic periodicity for Families A and B would imply Conjecture 1 of the cited prior work.
353823.source_name: Paul Ellis and Thotsaporn Aek Thanatipanonda, “The Arithmetic-Periodicity of cut for C=\1,2c\”, arXiv:2203.02457 (2022).

353871.title: Turán number conjecture for Cartesian products of trees
353871.literal_statement:
Let $T$ and $S$ be trees, each with at least one edge, and let $T\Box S$ denote their Cartesian product. For a positive integer $n$, let $\mathrm{ex}(n,T\Box S)$ be the maximum number of edges in a $(T\Box S)$-free graph on $n$ vertices. **Cartesian-product conjecture.** There exist positive real numbers $c$ and $C$ such that

$$
cn^{3/2}\leq \mathrm{ex}(n,T\Box S)\leq Cn^{3/2}.
$$

The product $T\Box S$ is $2$-degenerate, and the conjecture is motivated in part by Erdős's conjecture on Turán numbers of degenerate bipartite graphs. Its general validity remains open.
353871.source_name: Domagoj Bradač, Oliver Janzer, Benny Sudakov and István Tomon, “The Turán number of the grid”, arXiv:2203.05485 (2022).

353872.title: Turán bound conjecture for higher-dimensional grids
353872.literal_statement:
For positive integers $d$ and $t$, let $F_t^{(d)}$ be the $d$-dimensional grid with vertex set $[t]^d$, where two vertices are adjacent when they differ by exactly one in exactly one coordinate. For a positive integer $n$, let $\mathrm{ex}(n,F_t^{(d)})$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $F_t^{(d)}$-free graph on $n$ vertices. **Higher-dimensional grid conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,F_t^{(d)})\leq Cn^{2-1/d}.
$$

This is suggested by the fact that $F_t^{(d)}$ is $d$-degenerate and would extend the paper's two-dimensional grid result. The conjecture remains open in general.

353901.title: Negami's joint crossing number conjecture
353901.literal_statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be graphs embedded on a closed surface $S$, and let the **joint crossing number** be the minimum number of crossing points between $h(G_1)$ and $G_2$ over all homeomorphisms $h:S\to S$. **Negami's conjecture.** There exists a universal constant $C$ such that, for any such pair, the joint crossing number is at most

$$
C|E(G_1)||E(G_2)|.
$$

Negami proved an $O(g|E(G_1)||E(G_2)|)$ bound for graphs embedded on a closed surface of genus $g$. The conjecture would give a genus-independent bound and is equivalent to the existence of short decompositions of any fixed topological shape; it remains open.
353901.source_name: Niloufar Fuladi, Alfredo Hubard and Arnaud de Mesmay, “Short Topological Decompositions of Non-Orientable Surfaces”, arXiv:2203.06659 (2022).

353923.title: The leafless vertex metric dimension bound conjecture
353923.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph distinct from the cycle $C_n$, with minimum degree $\delta(G)\geq2$. Here $\mathrm{dim}(G)$ denotes the vertex metric dimension and $c(G)$ the cyclomatic number. The **leafless vertex metric dimension bound conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{dim}(G)\leq2c(G)-1.
$$

The bound is known for leafless cactus graphs, and the source proves it for $\Theta$-graphs; the general case reduces to 2-connected graphs distinct from cycles and remains open.

353924.title: The equality characterization for leafless vertex metric dimension
353924.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with minimum degree $\delta(G)\geq2$. A **daisy graph** is a graph consisting of at least two cycles sharing one vertex, and a petal is one of its cycles; $\Theta_{p,q,r}$ denotes the corresponding theta graph with three internally disjoint paths of lengths $p,q,r$. The **leafless vertex metric dimension equality conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{dim}(G)=2c(G)-1
$$

if and only if $G$ is a daisy graph without odd petals, $G=\Theta_{p,p,p}$, or $G=\Theta_{p,p,p+2}$. The source presents this as an expected characterization; it is proved only for the classes treated in the paper, so the general statement remains open.
353924.source_name: Martin Knor, Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “Remarks on the vertex and the edge metric dimension of 2-connected graphs”, arXiv:2203.07335 (2022).

354003.title: The precise 2-adic valuation conjecture for Eisenstein-series coefficients
354003.literal_statement:
Let $w_{a,k}$ be the coefficients defined by the expansion referred to as equation (w), let $\nu_2$ denote the 2-adic valuation, and let $s(k)$ denote the notation used in the source. For an even integer $k\geq 4$,

\min_a\bigl(\nu_2(w_{a,k})\bigr)=\begin{cases}s(k)-2&\text{if }k\neq 2^j,\\0&\text{if }k=2^j.
\end{cases}

354038.title: The rainbow Sidon-coloring conjecture
354038.literal_statement: Let $r\ge 2$ be an integer and let $n$ be sufficiently large. An $r$-coloring of a subset of $[n]$ is **rainbow $[1,-1,1,-1]$-free** if it contains no rainbow $4$-element set satisfying the corresponding linear equation. **The rainbow Sidon-coloring conjecture.** Among all subsets of $[n]$, the full set $[n]$ is the unique subset admitting the maximum number of rainbow $[1,-1,1,-1]$-free $r$-colorings. In particular, almost all rainbow $[1,-1,1,-1]$-free $r$-colorings of $[n]$ use at most $3$ colors. This is motivated by the connection between $[1,-1,1,-1]$-free sets and Sidon sets, and predicts both extremality of the full interval and a three-color concentration phenomenon for almost all such colorings.
354038.source_name: Hao Lin, Guanghui Wang and Wenling Zhou, “Integer colorings with no rainbow k-term arithmetic progression”, arXiv:2203.12735 (2022).

354081.title: Tilde-theta algorithmic-threshold conjecture for the symmetric binary perceptron
354081.literal_statement:
Let $kappa>0$ be the SBP parameter and let the algorithmic threshold be the largest constraint density up to which efficient algorithms can find a solution with high probability. **Tilde-theta threshold conjecture.** As $kappa\to0$, the algorithmic threshold for the SBP is at

$$
\widetilde{Theta}(kappa^2).
$$

The paper establishes an $m$-OGP obstruction at densities of order $kappa^2log_2(1/kappa)$ and an efficient algorithm at densities of order $kappa^2$, leaving only polylogarithmic factors between the known bounds.

354087.title: Sudakov's bipartisation conjecture for K_{r+1}-free graphs
354087.literal_statement:
For a graph $G$, let $D_2(G)$ be the minimum number of edges that must be deleted to make $G$ bipartite. Fix $r\geq3$, and let $G$ be an $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graph. **Sudakov's bipartisation conjecture.**

$$
D_2(G)\leq\begin{cases}\frac{(r-1)^2}{4r^2}n^2,& r\text{ odd},\\frac{r-2}{4r}n^2,& r\text{ even}.\end{cases}
$$
 The conjecture is known for $r=5$ by flag algebras, whereas the even-$r$ cases are described as more difficult and remain open.
354087.source_name: József Balogh, Felix Christian Clemen and Bernard Lidický, “10 Problems for Partitions of Triangle-free Graphs”, arXiv:2203.15764 (2022).

354118.title: O'Neill and Versträete's uniform extremal-family conjecture
354118.literal_statement:
Let $\binom{[n]}k$ be the family of $k$-element subsets of $[n]$. For $r\geq2$, let ${\rm BD}_r(n,k)$ and $\mathcal F_r(n,k,r-1)$ be the two specified non-trivial $r$-wise intersecting $k$-uniform families. A family is **extremal** if it has maximum size among non-trivial $r$-wise intersecting subfamilies of $\binom{[n]}k$.

**O'Neill and Versträete's conjecture.** Let $k>r\geq2$ and $n\geq kr(r-1)$. Then the unique extremal non-trivial $r$-wise intersecting families in $\binom{[n]}k$ are ${\rm BD}_r(n,k)$ and $\mathcal F_r(n,k,r-1)$, up to isomorphism.

This is the proposed uniform analogue of the extremal result for product-measure families. The supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture.
354118.source_name: Norihide Tokushige, “The maximum measure of non-trivial 3-wise intersecting families”, arXiv:2203.17158 (2023).

354171.title: Optimality of the constant-weight-code bounds for extremal designs in hypercubes
354171.literal_statement:
Let $Q_d$ be the $d$-dimensional hypercube. For each constant-weight code constructed in Lemma~, consider its dual under Gale duality, viewed as a positively weighted extremal design in $Q_d$.

**Optimality conjecture.** The duals of these constant-weight codes are smallest-cardinality positively weighted extremal designs in their respective hypercubes $Q_d$.

354173.title: The large-r feedback arc set conjecture for r-free digraphs
354173.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a digraph on $n$ vertices, let $\beta(G)$ denote the minimum size of a feedback arc set, and let an **$(r-1)$-free digraph** be one containing no directed cycle of length at most $r-1$. **Large-r feedback arc set conjecture.** If $G$ is an $(r-1)$-free digraph and $r>2n/3$, then

$$
\beta(G)\leq 1.
$$

The claim is presented as a more precise conjecture for the regime where $r$ is large relative to the number of vertices; no resolution is given.

354201.title: The distinct-primes principal-block set conjecture
354201.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $p$ and $q$ be primes dividing the order of $G$. For a prime $r$, write $B_r(G)$ for the principal $r$-block of $G$, and let $\operatorname{Irr}_{r'}(B_r(G))$ denote the irreducible complex characters in $B_r(G)$ whose degrees are not divisible by $r$. **The distinct-primes principal-block set conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{Irr}_{p'}(B_p(G))=\operatorname{Irr}_{q'}(B_q(G)),
$$

then $p=q$.

This asserts that the prime-indexed sets of nondivisible-degree characters in principal blocks determine the prime; the paper presents the claim among the proposed conjectures and gives supporting results, but does not resolve it in general.
354201.source_name: Gabriel Navarro, Noelia Rizo and A. A. Schaeffer Fry, “Principal blocks for different primes, II”, arXiv:2204.03130 (2022).

354205.title: Mutation invariance of unrestricted red size
354205.literal_statement:
Let $Q$ be a quiver and let $\mu_k(Q)$ denote the quiver obtained by mutation at vertex $k$. The **unrestricted red size** $\operatorname{uRed}(Q)$ is the minimum red size over general reddening sequences of $Q$. **Mutation-invariance conjecture.** The unrestricted red size is mutation invariant: 

$$
\operatorname{uRed}(Q)=\operatorname{uRed}(\mu_k(Q))
$$

for any $k$. This conjecture concerns the potential mutation invariance of the unrestricted red number; unlike the unrestricted red size, the existence of a maximal green sequence is not mutation invariant.
354205.source_name: Eric Bucher and John Machacek, “Red sizes of quivers”, arXiv:2204.03212 (2022).

354224.title: The crossing-degree conjecture for complete simple topological graphs
354224.literal_statement:
Let $h=h(n)$ be the smallest integer such that every complete $n$-vertex simple topological graph contains an edge crossing at most $h$ other edges. A **simple topological graph** is a graph drawn in the plane so that vertices are distinct points, edges are simple arcs joining their endpoints, no edge contains a vertex other than its endpoints, and every pair of edges intersects at most once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing.

**Crossing-degree conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that

$$
h(n)\leq n^{2-\varepsilon}.
$$

The source records the lower bound $h(n)=\Omega(n^{3/2})$ and upper bounds of order $n^2/(\log n)^{1/2-o(1)}$. The conjecture seeks a polynomial improvement over the quadratic upper bound and remains open.
354224.source_name: Andrew Suk and Ji Zeng, “Unavoidable patterns in complete simple topological graphs”, arXiv:2204.04293 (2022).

354231.title: Aharoni–Zerbib generalized Tuza conjecture for uniform hypergraphs
354231.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an $r$-graph. An $(r-1)$-matching is a set of edges such that any two intersect in fewer than $r-1$ vertices, and an $(r-1)$-cover is a collection of $(r-1)$-sets of vertices such that every edge contains one of them. Write $\nu^{(r-1)}(G)$ and $\tau^{(r-1)}(G)$ for the maximum size of an $(r-1)$-matching and the minimum size of an $(r-1)$-cover, respectively. **Aharoni–Zerbib generalized conjecture.** For any $r$-graph $G$,

$$
\tau^{(r-1)}(G) \leq \left\lceil \frac{r+1}{2} \right\rceil\nu^{(r-1)}(G).
$$

This conjecture extends the triangle-cover inequality to uniform hypergraphs. The paper proves it with high probability for $r\in\{3,4,5\}$ in the random model $H_r(n,p)$, while the deterministic assertion for general $r$ remains open.
354231.source_name: Abdul Basit and David Galvin, “Generalized Tuza's conjecture for random hypergraphs”, arXiv:2204.04568 (2024).

354258.title: The nonnegativity conjecture for Jones-slope coefficients
354258.literal_statement:
Let $K$ be a knot in $S^3$. Write the maximum and minimum colored-Jones degrees as quadratic quasi-polynomials

$$
\delta_K(n)=a(n)n^2+b(n)n+c(n),\qquad
\delta_K^*(n)=a^*(n)n^2+b^*(n)n+c^*(n).
$$

**Coefficient nonnegativity conjecture.** For any knot in $S^3$,

$$
a(n)\geq 0\quad\text{and}\quad a^*(n)\leq 0.
$$

The inequalities assert opposite signs for the leading coefficients of the maximum and minimum degrees, equivalently for the corresponding Jones slopes. The statement is presented as a conjectural general property; the paper proves it for several families and uses it in the study of Mazur doubles.
354258.source_name: Kenneth L. Baker, Kimihiko Motegi and Toshie Takata, “The Strong Slope Conjecture and crossing numbers for Mazur doubles of knots”, arXiv:2204.05725 (2022).

scc(G) \leq \frac{7}{5}|E(G)|.

354288.title: Merino–Welsh conjectures for matroids
354288.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid without loops and coloops, and let $T_M(x,y)$ denote its Tutte polynomial.

**Merino–Welsh conjectures.** The following three inequalities should hold:

$$
\max\left(T_M(2,0),T_M(0,2)\right)\geq T_M(1,1),
$$

$$
T_M(2,0)+T_M(0,2)\geq 2T_M(1,1),
$$

$$
T_M(2,0)T_M(0,2)\geq T_M(1,1)^2.
$$

These are respectively the maximum, additive, and multiplicative versions of the graph conjecture. The multiplicative inequality implies the additive one, which implies the maximum inequality. The conjectures are known for several classes, including lattice path matroids and paving matroids for the additive version, while the general matroidal claims remain open.
354288.source_name: Luis Ferroni and Benjamin Schröter, “The Merino–Welsh conjecture for split matroids”, arXiv:2204.07132 (2022).

354296.title: Regular Cereceda's Conjecture
354296.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph, let $\mu(G)$ denote its matching number, let $n(G)$ denote its number of vertices, and let $\mathcal{C}_k(G)$ be the reconfiguration graph of proper $k$-colourings of $G$.

**Regular Cereceda's Conjecture.** If $k=d+2$, then

$$
\operatorname{diam} \mathcal{C}_k(G)=n(G)+\mu(G).
$$

This would combine the conjectured upper bound for list-colouring reconfiguration with the corresponding lower-bound question to determine the precise diameter at the threshold for regular graphs. It remains open.

354307.title: Canonical bijection between degenerate tetrahedra and planar quadruples
354307.literal_statement: A quadruple of points in the special affine plane determines triangle and Varignon-parallelogram areas. Consider the corresponding quadruple of Euclidean-plane points for which the radius of gyration $R_\mathsf G$ attains its unique minimum subject to preserving those areas. Let degenerate tetrahedra be the tetrahedra defined by the zeros of $\Omega$. **Canonical-bijection conjecture.** The bijection between affine-plane quadruples and the corresponding minimizing Euclidean-plane quadruples extends to a bijection between the set of degenerate tetrahedra and the set of all quadruples in the Euclidean plane; moreover, this mapping is, or can be chosen to be, canonical, so that the two sets can be identified.

354337.title: The explicit Brumer–Stark unit conjecture via Shintani integrals
354337.literal_statement:
Let $F$ be a totally real field, let $H/F$ be a finite abelian CM extension, and let $\mathfrak p$ split completely in $H$. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak b$ prime to the prescribed modulus, let $\sigma_{\mathfrak b}\in G$ be its Frobenius and let $u_p(\mathfrak b)^{\mathrm{an}}\in F_p^*$ be the explicitly defined multiplicative-integral expression. Let $u_{\mathfrak p}$ be the Brumer–Stark unit. **Explicit Brumer–Stark unit conjecture.** One should have 
$$
\sigma_{\mathfrak b}(u_{\mathfrak p})=u_p(\mathfrak b)^{\mathrm{an}}\quad\text{in }F_p^*.
$$
 The formula is intended to compute all conjugates of the Brumer–Stark unit and has computational applications to explicit class field theory. The source gives no resolution status.
354337.source_name: Samit Dasgupta and Mahesh Kakde, “On the Brumer-Stark Conjecture and Refinements”, arXiv:2204.09037 (2022).

354368.title: The conjectured value of the line-piercing number $L(k)$
354368.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of compact, convex sets in the plane, and let $L(k)$ denote the minimum number of lines guaranteed to pierce $\mathcal{F}$ when $\mathcal{F}$ contains no $C(k)$, where $C(k)$ is a family of $k$ sets $F_1,\dots,F_k$ such that

$$
\operatorname{conv}(F_i\cup F_{i+1})\cap \operatorname{conv}(F_j\cup F_{j+1})=\emptyset
$$

whenever $\{i,i+1\}\cap\{j,j+1\}=\emptyset$, with indices taken modulo $k$. **The conjecture for $L(k)$.** We have

$$
L(k)=\left\lceil \frac{k}{2} \right\rceil.
$$

The paper explains that this is the conjectured correct value because it matches the lower bound proved in the main theorem; the source does not specify whether the conjecture has been resolved.
354368.source_name: Daniel McGinnis, “Piercing families of convex sets in the plane that avoid a certain subfamily with lines”, arXiv:2204.10490 (2022).

354369.title: The positivity and real-rootedness conjecture for increasing-subsequence character polynomials
354369.literal_statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $\textnormal{id}_k=12\ldots k\in S_k$ be the identity permutation, and let $M_{\textnormal{id}_k,n}$ be the $n$-th moment class function associated with occurrences of the increasing pattern $\textnormal{id}_k$. For a partition $\lambda$, let $a_{\textnormal{id}_k}^\lambda(n)$ be the polynomial agreeing with the irreducible-character coefficient $\langle\chi^{\lambda[n]},M_{\textnormal{id}_k,n}\rangle$ whenever defined.

**Positivity and real-rootedness conjecture.** For all $k,n\in\mathbb{N}$, $M_{\textnormal{id}_k,n}$ is a nonnegative linear combination of irreducible symmetric group characters. Furthermore, the polynomials $a_{\textnormal{id}_k}^\lambda(n)$ are real-rooted, with all roots less than $k$.

This conjecture combines a positivity assertion for the character expansion of the increasing-subsequence moment with a root-location assertion for its stable character coefficients. It is the main motivation of the paper; the surrounding results establish polynomiality of the coefficients, while the stated positivity and real-rootedness remain conjectural.
354369.source_name: Christian Gaetz and Laura Pierson, “Positivity of permutation pattern character polynomials”, arXiv:2204.10633 (2024).

354385.title: Uniqueness conjecture for generalized Markov numbers
354385.literal_statement:
For each pair $(q,p)in \mathbb Z_{>0}^2$ with $q\geq p$, let $m_{q,p}$ denote the generalized Markov number associated with $(q,p)$. **Uniqueness conjecture for generalized Markov numbers.** For any $(q,p),(q',p')\in \mathbb Z_{>0}^2$ with $q\geq p$ and $q'\geq p'$, if $(q,p)\neq(q',p')$, then

$$
m_{q,p}\neq m_{q',p'}.
$$

This conjecture asserts that distinct admissible pairs determine distinct generalized Markov numbers. The source proposes it after discussing monotonicity, but gives no resolution evidence.
354385.source_name: Min Huang, “On the monotonicity of the generalized Markov numbers”, arXiv:2204.11443 (2022).
